name: Pseudopelade of Brocq

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and histopathological criteria for Pseudopelade of Brocq

criteria.description: Presence of multiple irregular, smooth, flesh-colored, atrophic patches of scalp alopecia
Minimal or absent clinical inflammation and absence of follicular pustules
Histopathological evidence of scarring alopecia with loss of hair follicles and replacement by fibrous tracts
Negative autoimmune serology to exclude lupus erythematosus and lichen planopilaris

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical patch, absence of inflammation, histopathology) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by biopsy; exclusion of other scarring alopecias is essential

laboratory: Negative autoimmune serology (ANA, anti-dsDNA) to exclude lupus erythematosus
Normal complete blood count and inflammatory markers
imaging: Trichoscopy showing absence of follicular openings and white fibrotic areas
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified
other: Histopathology demonstrating follicular dropout with replacement fibrosis and absence of significant inflammation

distinguishingFeatures: Erythematous, scaly plaques with follicular plugging
More common in women of African descent

redFlags: Presence of pustules or significant scalp inflammation
Systemic symptoms such as fever or malaise
references: Miteva M, Tosti A. Pseudopelade of Brocq: a review. Int J Trichology. 2013;5(1):1-6.
Whiting DA. Cicatricial alopecia: clinico-pathological findings and treatment. Dermatol Clin. 1996;14(4):697-713.
